pr_body:
# `.ConfigureAwait(false)` in SignalR client libraries

- Enable `CA2007` (Consider calling ConfigureAwait on the awaited task) for SignalR client libraries and shared libraries
- Don't use `ForceAsync()` in ignalR client libraries and shared libraries
  - The previous use of `ForceAsync()` could still cause deadlocks of the code using the client tried to block a UI thread (or any one-at-a-time `SynchronizationContext`) because internal SignalR logic would try to post back to it.

Fixes #39626
Partially addresses #31132

@BrennanConroy I made a repo out of my zip: https://github.com/Kolky/signalr-bug

Ok, ~~so you're running the server and the client in the same process and~~ since you're using WPF you are running in a "single-threaded" environment. What this means is that when you stop ~~the server~~ via exiting the app, you run on the UI thread and block any asynchronous work also running on the UI thread from completing. In this case you run `Example.StopAsync()` inline and hang your app.

I don't know the proper way to handle async work in WPF, but a quick fix is to replace `_host.WaitForShutdown()` with `Task.Run(() => _host.WaitForShutdownAsync().ConfigureAwait(false)).ConfigureAwait(false).GetAwaiter().GetResult();`
Sounds like this isn't a SignalR issue, so I'll mark this as resolved.
